data: A compact primitive model: Ø100 × 10 flange, Ø44 × 16 hub, Ø24 bore and six Ø9 bolt holes on a 70 mm PCD.
An XZ polygon extruded along Y with an edge fillet and two native SolidCraft Hole features.

One shared CornerBracket is reused by the standalone model and wooden HUB75 assemblies. Its native outline includes the 0.6 mm arm-tip relief, with inner R4 fillet, broad-face chamfers and four local triangular arm-tip wedge cuts kept editable. Four fixing seats use separate flat head recess, 90° transition, through-bore and 0.2 mm edge-relief features instead of one oversized countersink.
A constructive solid geometry demonstration: intersect a cube with a sphere, then subtract cylinders along three axes.

A printable bench dog inferred from the Mini-MFT reference image: 20 mm above and 20 mm below the worktop, with one full-length tapered insert from Ø20.0 at the worktop to Ø20.2 at the free end. A compact Ø22 stop collar seats on the 45° chamfer of a nominal Ø20 MFT hole. Two perpendicular slots create four flexible legs, with R0.5 mm relief around the central cross. The top face carries a recessed BrainBox cube/box wireframe.

A second fixed cross-section of the generic GuideRail component. The aluminium shape comes from the Makita 199141-8 STEP reference and is calibrated to the TSO measured 182.50 × 10.28 mm envelope. The standalone CAD example uses 600 mm for compact visual inspection.

The generic GuideRail component with its default Festool profile. The aluminium cross-section comes from the FS 1400/2 STEP reference and is calibrated to the TSO measured 184.20 × 10.50 mm envelope. Only rail length is a native CAD parameter.

Second-generation wooden HUB75 enclosure. It keeps the 844 × 362 mm display opening and five-panel layout while adding a 70 mm clear lower compartment, a 12 mm intermediate shelf, two 12 mm dividers, full-depth side walls with hand slots, and an inset display-only rear board.

Shared panel component from the existing OpenSCAD reference: a 159.70 × 319.71 × 14.50 mm envelope with four rear pockets, six rear-side Ø3 bores in Ø8.5 mounting tubes, separate rear reinforcement features, two locator pins and a grey housing material. Standalone uses the component’s own local XY/Z axes; screen assemblies rotate the exact same class into world XZ.

Five panels on the source project’s 800 × 320 mm nominal grid. One reusable detailed panel component is reused at X=-320, -160, 0, 160 and 320 mm. Columns 2 and 4 reverse direction for the rear data chain, and all occurrences stand upright in XZ.

One clearly parametrized assembly: five lightweight HUB75 modules, 12 mm sidewalls/bottom/roof, 9 mm attached rear, 4 mm glass and four straight-mitred wooden retainers from one GlassStrip class. The roof extends 10 mm in front and 1 mm beyond the attached rear sheet. Eight printed corner brackets share the CornerBracket definition.

A reusable light mounting-rail component modelled as native sheet metal. The supplied DRESSELHAUS/HORNBACH product establishes 1000 mm length, galvanized steel, M8 use and 1.25 mm thickness. The 27 × 18 mm C-profile and perforation dimensions use a generic published 27/18 rail reference and are not claimed as DRESSELHAUS manufacturing dimensions.
Reconstructs the Raspberry Pi 4 video using a rounded open-top shell, mounting bosses, connector cuts, floor vents, Pi 4 lettering and PETG material.
Rebuilds the supplied enclosure with the normal SCPF Box sketch/extrusion, followed by native Shell, Lip, Snap Fit, Boss and Rest features.
A feature-based plate: box, four vertical fillets and four through holes.
Builds a centered plate with native Base, Holes and Bore sketches. One parameter-driven Ø8 hole cut is repeated by a native rectangular pattern, while a Ø24 boss is joined between the two cuts.
Minimal model proving that one independent model root can be authored with Forge and built without repository-specific Python orchestration.

An assembly that reuses the standalone Simple MFT component and the generic GuideRail component. The rail runs along the short Y/depth direction, is centred over X=0 and rests on the parametrically shared worktop top face.

A reusable CRAFTMAKER-inspired worktop component: one 18 mm native Box, four straight 20 mm corner chamfers, 59 Ø20 dog holes on the nominal 9 × 7 / 76 mm grid with the four diagonal ring-2 positions omitted, and eight photo-measured native diagonal Slots.
Recreates the SolidCraft Vent Plate example with a rounded 120 × 80 × 4 mm plate, one rectangular source cut and one native two-direction rectangular pattern.
